utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Your Honour, case number IT-97-25/1-PT, the Prosecutor against Mitar Rasevic and Savo Todovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, appearing for the Prosecution together with case manager Helena Tavares-Borges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will ask the Defence counsel to introduce themselves, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Vladimir Domazet, counsel representing Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I am Aleksandar Lazarevic, counsel for Mr. Todovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to welcome all the people present in the courtroom; the registrar who is helping us today, I would like to welcome the usher, the representative of the Prosecution, the legal officer, and the two Defence counsels, as well as Mr. Rasevic who is also attending this hearing. I have not forgotten to mention the interpreters who are giving us a helping hand this morning. As you know, this is a Status Conference. Mr. Rasevic is the sole accused to attend this hearing today. Mr. Todovic let us know that he was unable to come for medical reasons. He therefore shall be represented today by Mr. Lazarevic. As you know, according to Article 68 bis, the Trial Chamber must convene a hearing every 120 days so that -- to facilitate exchange between the parties and to -- so that I can assess the situation and see that this trial does not run late. As you know, on the 4th of November, 2004, motions had been filed pursuant to Rule 11 bis to refer this case to Bosnia-Herzegovina. Following these motions a -- this has been referred to the Tribunal of Bosnia-Herzegovina pursuant to Article 11 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Following this decision, the accused Todovic and the accused Rasevic have applied -- have appealed the decision taken -- decision for referral. Eight months have passed now, and the Appeals Chamber has been seized of this appeal and to date no decision has been rendered yet. The Prosecution could perhaps let us know where the procedure stands and where we stand vis-a-vis the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually, what you said is correct. All that's -- I don't know more than that; that is, the appeal is still pending. And I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall wait for the Appeals Chamber to render a decision. Either it will confirm the decision and the case is referred to Bosnia-Herzegovina or the case is not confirmed, in which case it would be tried before this Tribunal. This is all the more important as, as you know, the accused Todovic had filed a motion pursuant to Rule 72(A) pertaining to the form of the indictment, and this motion for the time being has not -- the Trial Chamber has not rendered a decision vis-a-vis this particular motion. As far as I'm concerned, I feel that if the case is referred to a Tribunal in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Prosecutor in that country is -- can then draft the indictment and refer it to the competent authorities. So I don't see what the purpose of rendering a decision thereof on a particular legal issue; i.e., the form of the indictment, if it is being referred to another jurisdiction. However, if the Appeals Chamber hands down a decision which sets aside this particular issue, in that case -- and if this is to be tried before this Tribunal, in that case we will have enough time to respond to this motion. This does not raise any particular problem, because as you know, a judgement has already been handed down by the Appeals Chamber in the Krnojelac case. A decision pertaining to the form of the indictment has already been rendered following the motion filed by the accused Rasevic. So, as things stand today, we already have the legal basis enabling us to render a decision on the merits of the filed by Mr. Todovic. At this stage of the hearing I notice that this -- a decision could have been taken a while ago, but as things stand, no decision has been taken yet. It's also important to note that in the case the -- this case would be referred to a national jurisdiction pursuant to Rule 11 bis and Rule 10 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the Prosecution will be entitled to follow the proceedings and may ask the national jurisdiction to be disqualified, which would yet again extend the dead-line. So I cannot tell Mr. Rasevic when he will be tried before a court because I have no power of decision on the dead-lines. As I had already stipulated a while ago already, that this case could have been tried a year and a half already ago. At this stage, pursuant to Rule 66(A) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, I must mention the issue of disclosure of material. I took stock of the situation a while ago, I don't think there is any particular problem here. All the material has been disclosed, and I don't think anything special needs to be mentioned here. The same applies to Rule 68; I think everything has been disclosed and I think that has been settled. If there are no particular issues arising out of Rule 66 and 68, I would like to address the additional issue of the computer which Todovic has been provided with. In October 2005 Mr. Lazarevic told us that his client did not have a computer in his cell. I investigated the matter, and this is a fairly relevant issue, given that over the last few months we have now -- we now have an EDS system, which can be used by the accused in the Detention Centre, and electronic disclosure can only be carried out by using this -- by using a computer, but in order for this to work, the accused have to have a computer. If they don't have a computer, I don't see how the system could work. So Mr. Lazarevic will tell me about this, but from what I understand, the accused Todovic still does not have a computer because there is a problem with the computer company that was supposed to provide the computer. The contract with the said company still hasn't been signed and therefore the accused is still without a computer. Mr. Lazarevic, could you confirm this, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By all means, Your Honour. The PC that is currently waiting in the Detention Unit for Mr. Todovic was brought in The Hague by myself and I believe that he could work on this computer, although it is mine, however the situation that appeared seems that a company was called to provide with computers all the detainees and so far it hasn't been performed, so Mr. Todovic still does not have a PC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I know that Mr. Todovic still doesn't have a computer but I don't think he is the only one to be in that position. A number of other accused do not have a computer either. That said, some of the accused had been given a computer by family members, but these cannot be used because in the meantime it has been decided that the accused must use the computers provided by the Registry. So let's wait for this computer to reach the accused. There is no reason for despair, and I'm sure there will be a positive outcome here. Before I give the floor to Mr. Rasevic, does the Prosecution have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lazarevic, would you like to add anything, specify anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that Your Honour is already informed regarding Mr. Todovic's medical condition. I would just like to give one further explanation. Mr. Todovic broke his arm, and he had a minor surgery yesterday, and that is the only reason why he couldn't attend this Status Conference, and I was asked by Mr. Todovic to tell this before the Trial Chamber. He has no complaints regarding medical treatment, I have to say this. However, I will follow closely the development of his medical problem and if -- in any case I will inform the Trial Chamber in case of an emergency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Domazet, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as Mr. Rasevic is concerned, there is no problem. The sole problem being that we are just awaiting the decision. He would also like to say that there is no particular problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rasevic, could you stand up, please. I have two questions to put to you regarding your health. Is there anything special you would like to mention or not? THE ACCUSED RASEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there are no problems regarding my medical condition. In that respect everything is perfect, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. The second question relates to your conditions in detention. Do you have any complaints to file or any comments to make? THE ACCUSED RASEVIC: [Interpretation] As far as the conditions in the Detention Unit, from the very first day I didn't have any complaints and the situation in that respect is also perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, thank you. Would you like to say anything about any other topic? THE ACCUSED RASEVIC: [Interpretation] Please allow me just to say one or two sentences. It's a personal thing. I've spent already two and a half years here, so I would first of all like to thank you for treating me fairly. I see you have put it already eight months have passed since the beginning of the 11 bis proceedings appeal. I have at first talked with my Defence about my wishes and I said I did not wish to raise an appeal because in that way maybe the decision would have been expedited. I do not care really personally which Tribunal will be trying me, I believe that any Tribunal will do its job in accordance with the law and the evidence. I believe that this court in Sarajevo will deal with me in the same manner, therefore I do not see why is it necessary for this to be postponed for a period of eight months. It's a simple decision to make. I will either be tried here or not. This way this is being postponed and postponed again, nothing is happening there, we are waiting for one thing to get settled, but then things grind to a halt, we have to start again, and then we have to wait for something else. I would like to ask, therefore, both the Chamber and Madam Prosecutor, can you somehow please ask them to expedite this issue so that it's sorted out in a reasonable time-frame? This is my request. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Rasevic. I shall let the Appeals Chamber know what you have just said, and I shall ask them to take their decision speedily. As you have just indicated, you have been waiting for the last eight months for this final decision. I would like to thank you, you may sit down. I hope that we will not need to see each other again, because if we meet again this will be in 120 days' time. I hope that in the mean time everything will be settled. As I have just said, I shall, as I have committed to, inform the Appeals Chamber of this particular situation. If there are no other issues to be raised, I would like to thank you. And the court stands adjourned.
